## 🔴 High Relevance (Score 7–10)
*Auto-added to Zotero (threshold ≥6)*

**[The IKK complex and TBK1/IKKε are recruited to STING through distinct mechanisms to activate NF-κB signaling.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42853962/)** *(from Innate immunology / evolutionary cell signaling biology (ubiquitin biology))*  
*Christensen Anna Hvarregaard; Jurkiewicz Aneta J; Jensen Cathrine Silberbauer; K* — Science immunology 2026  
Score: **7/10** | Pathways: `cGAS-STING, NF-kB-IKK, NF-kB-NLRP3-priming, treatment-target`  
> The paper shows that STING activates NF-κB through M1-linked ubiquitin-dependent recruitment of NEMO/IKKγ and the IKK complex, with TBK1/IKKε acting independently of IRF3. This is the STING-NEMO NF-κB axis in the disease model, and it is the route by which chronic cGAS-STING signaling from SAMHD1 haploinsufficiency would prime NLRP3 and pro-IL-1β and drive inflammatory output separately from IFN-I. It offers a possible anti-inflammatory target that spares IRF3, but it has no SAMHD1, mitochondrial, or NLRP3 data, so it is a novel-mechanism paper on one core pathway rather than direct disease evidence.  
DOI: 10.1126/sciimmunol.aeh5148

**[SAMHD1 dysfunction drives microglial phagocytosis of PS-exposing vulnerable neurons via the GAS6-AXL axis in Aicardi-Goutières syndrome.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42849603/)** *(from Neurology/neuroscience (microglial biology, neurodegeneration))*  
*Cui Jiuhao; Shen Ziyang; Liu Hancheng; Chen Ting; Zhang Ling* — Experimental neurology 2026  
Score: **7/10** | Pathways: `AGS-spectrum, other, treatment-target, clinical-phenotype`  
> Demonstrates that SAMHD1 deficiency (rat knockout, microglial knockdown) drives a GAS6-AXL-PI3K/AKT microglial phagocytosis axis and neuronal loss in AGS, a novel SAMHD1 mechanism with a potential neuro-inflammatory therapeutic target (AXL inhibition) relevant to the family's neurodevelopmental phenotypes (AuDHD, dystonia). It is a complete-loss model rather than A565T heterozygous haploinsufficiency, and it does not address the cGAS-STING, NLRP3, or mitochondrial streams.  
DOI: 10.1016/j.expneurol.2026.116057

**[Exercise promotes host anti-infection activity through CNDP2 metabolite-mediated inflammasome hyperactivation.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42853862/)** *(from Exercise physiology / infectious disease (host defense))*  
*Qian Yan; Cheng Xiangyun; Liu Qiannv; Wang Chunlei; Kong Chun* — PLoS pathogens 2026  
Score: **7/10** | Pathways: `NLRP3, POLG-mtDNA, ME-CFS, treatment-target, other`  
> The paper shows that exercise drives a hyperactivated NLRP3 inflammasome state in which CypD/GSDMD interaction, limited mtDNA leakage and a CNDP2-derived γ-Glu-Cys metabolite act as mitochondrial-inflammasome control points. This bears directly on the mtDNA-to-NLRP3 loop (Loop B) and suggests a CypD-targeted modulatory approach. It also bears on exercise tolerance and post-exertional malaise in this ME/CFS-affected family. There is no SAMHD1, dNTP or interferon data, so the connection is mechanistic and indirect.  
DOI: 10.1371/journal.ppat.1014554

**[Bidirectional Crosstalk Between cGAS-STING and Necroptosis: From Mitochondrial DNA Release to Inflammatory Disease](https://doi.org/10.2147/dddt.s649776)** *(from Cell death biology / pharmacology (necroptosis, drug design), with links to neurodegeneration and oncology)*  
*Hong-Quan Wang; Zhi-Ji Wang; Hui Zhang; Zhi-Hang Yang; Shu-Lin Zhao* — Drug Design, Development and Therapy 2026  
Score: **7/10** | Pathways: `cGAS-STING, NF-kB-IKK, treatment-target, VDAC1, POLG-mtDNA, other`  
> Review of the cGAS-STING and necroptosis feed-forward loop, driven by mitochondrial damage and mtDNA release with type I IFN/TNF-α synergy and ZBP1 upregulation. It maps onto the family's Loop A (mtDNA escape, cGAS, STING, IFN-I) and the chronic interferonopathy amplification, and it covers STING/MLKL inhibitors and mitochondrial-protective strategies. It has no SAMHD1, dNTP or NLRP3-specific data, so the link is mechanistic and indirect.  
DOI: 10.2147/dddt.s649776

**[NET-derived DNA is associated with cGAS-STING and type I IFN responses, as supported by monocyte stimulation cultures using plasma from female patients with SLE.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42843114/)** *(from Rheumatology (SLE, autoimmunity))*
